svg.aria-label: Before and after comparison showing escape analysis erasing an Integer box, measured on Oracle JDK 21.0.7 on macOS aarch64. The left half is the non-escaping case: stakeTotalMinorUnits boxes a cash and a bonus stake amount in minor units, adds them and returns; C2 proves neither box escapes, so both are scalar-replaced and the two int values live in named register slots with no surrounding object, no 12-byte header, no int value field, and both Integer.valueOf and intValue folded away. Measured allocation is zero bytes over five million calls, and zero bytes at the QuizStakes scale of 2.8 million stake reservations per day; with escape analysis disabled the same code allocates 160,000,000 bytes, 32 bytes per iteration, which is two 16-byte Integer objects. The right half is the escaping case: stakeTotalAudited stores the same box into a static List of Integer named AUDIT on the ledger audit path, so the reference outlives the method and cannot be scalar-replaced. One 16-byte Integer is allocated per iteration, drawn as an object with an 8-byte mark word, a 4-byte compressed class word and a 4-byte int value, a total of 16 bytes already a multiple of 8 so no padding. Measured 80,000,000 bytes over five million iterations, 16 bytes per iteration, unchanged whether escape analysis is on or off; at 2.8 million stake reservations per day that is 2,800,000 times 16 equals 44,800,000 bytes, or 42.72 mebibytes of boxing per day on the audit path. Two annotation panels below give the full measured allocation table and the C2 flag values, plus a second measurement in which a Long accumulator over a one-million-element int array allocated 24,000,000 bytes, 24 bytes per iteration.
svg.text: Escape analysis erases a box — the same Integer, unpublished vs. published to the audit path
BEFORE / LEFT — NO ESCAPE: THE BOX IS SCALAR-REPLACED
AFTER / RIGHT — ESCAPES INTO AUDIT: ONE 16-BYTE OBJECT PER ITERATION
FundsLedger.stakeTotalMinorUnits — box never published
FundsLedger.stakeTotalAudited — box published to the ledger audit list

g.text: static final List<Integer> AUDIT = new ArrayList<>();

svg.text: C2 verdict: NO ESCAPE
both references die inside the method → EliminateAllocations fires
neither box is ever reachable from outside the compiled frame
C2 verdict: GLOBAL ESCAPE
the reference is stored into a static, GC-reachable collection on the
ledger's audit path — no scalar replacement is possible
SCALAR-REPLACED FORM — FIELDS LIVE IN REGISTERS, NO OBJECT
r19 : cashMinorUnits
plain int, 4 bytes, in a register
r20 : bonusMinorUnits
plain int, 4 bytes, in a register

g.text: Integer.valueOf(…) folded away — no invokestatic emitted
intValue() folded away — no invokevirtual emitted
no 12-byte header, no int value field, no heap object at all
the add executes directly on the two int registers
heap objects created per call: NONE
the box existed only in the bytecode; C2 deleted it before codegen

svg.text: ONE Integer PER ITERATION, KEPT LIVE BY AUDIT
AUDIT : List<Integer>
static, GC-reachable root
Integer instance on the heap
mark word .................. 8 bytes
class word (compressed) .... 4 bytes
int value .................. 4 bytes
= 16 bytes, a multiple of 8 already
so no padding is inserted

g.text: escape analysis cannot scalar-replace a box stored into a live collection —
the reference outlives the method, so the object must exist on the heap
measured 16.0 bytes per iteration with -XX:+DoEscapeAnalysis AND with it off
values are well outside −128..127, so IntegerCache never supplies the box

bool DoEscapeAnalysis = true {C2 product} {default} bool EliminateAllocations = true {C2 product} {default}
Long sum = 0L; for (int v : stakeMinorUnits) sum += v; over a 1,000,000-element int[] allocated a measured 24,000,000 bytes
= 24 bytes per iteration, one Long per +=, because the accumulator box is reassigned inside the loop; Long is 24 bytes (12-byte header + 4 padding + 8-byte long)
